name: Brack
desc: Fifty-six. Ran the yard for thirty years. Says less than he knows and knows more than he says.
tags: 1boy, solo, old man, bald, grey hair, mustache, facial hair, crooked nose, large man, tattoo on arm, anchor tattoo, gold ring
wear_tags: clean canvas apron, brass buckle, rolled shirtsleeves, neat
canvas apron, brass buckle, rolled shirtsleeves, sweat on the brow, flushed
stained canvas apron, brass buckle, grimy rolled shirtsleeves, dirty forearms, breathing hard
canvas apron torn off one shoulder, brass buckle hanging loose, bandaged forearm, shirt untucked, exhausted
canvas apron in tatters, bloodied shirt, bandaged forearm soaked through, cut above the eye, trembling, utterly exhausted
note: MEASURED: THE APRON DID NOT RENDER, AND THAT IS THIS CARD'S MAIN RESULT. Every rung of his ladder names a canvas apron, and the sheet plus all 16 turnaround views rendered BLUE DENIM DUNGAREES instead - bib, straps and all. 'canvas apron, brass buckle' was resolved by animagine into overalls with brass anchor buckles, merging the apron with the separately-requested anchor tattoo. The garment noun failed even though it was in the correct slot and in its clean state, which is a caution against assuming that wear_tags alone fixes the uniform problem: the ladder has to name a garment the engine can actually draw. An apron is apparently not one. | ALSO MEASURED: 'bald' BEAT 'grey hair'. He is meant to have a bald crown with a grey horseshoe fringe around the sides; he rendered completely bald in all 17 images. Two tags that a person reads as compatible are read by the model as a contradiction, and the earlier and more specific one won. Either drop 'bald' and say 'balding' or accept a bare scalp. | WHAT DID HOLD, across all 16 views: the heavy build, the full grey moustache, the forearm tattoos, the brass anchor hardware and the face. He is strongly consistent - he simply is not wearing what the card says. | NO LoRA. He was turned around but not trained; NIKA and PIP were the two training targets. His dataset is on disk at ~/ComfyUI/input/brack_train (16 pairs) if anyone wants the third. | AUTHORED AS THE FIX FOR A COMPLAINT WRITTEN INTO SIX TEMPLATE CARDS. argument_small_room, bad_news, confession, lonely_night_city, quiet_aftermath and reconciliation all warn that without a wear_tags override their characters will argue in uniform, because compose.py:1680 falls back to the WEAR constant, whose vocabulary is entirely sports kit. Nothing in his ladder is a uniform: it is an apron, and it fails the way an apron fails - stained, torn off one shoulder, in tatters. | Whether this actually fixes those six templates is UNVERIFIED - it needs one of them compiled and rendered, which was outside this pass. | base_tags is set even though MALE would have been harmless for him, because the constant hard-codes build as well as sex and he is heavy; 'heavyset' replaces a default that says nothing about build. | THE GARMENT LIVES IN wear_tags, NOT IN tags. | `prose` is the VISUAL description used by the qwen engine; `desc` is narrative and tells an image model nothing it can draw.
prose: a heavyset man in his fifties, bald on top with a grey horseshoe fringe around the sides, a full grey moustache, a nose flattened at the bridge, an anchor tattoo on his right forearm, a gold ring on his left little finger
